question: What finite storage and request ordering does the selected native UI event queue implement, and what does its count fail to establish about append, delivery and which code holds, replaces and releases what the queue stores?

scope.qualification: The listed producer, growth, error and reader windows define the selected scope. Three leaves have no asserted PE extent. Other helper descendants and dispatcher branches retain their separate contracts or unresolved effects.

storageBoundary.base: P denotes the manager argument to 0x82C56388. At 0x82C563BC the working pointer becomes D=P+0x18. Queue map M=U32[D+4]=U32[P+0x1C], block capacity B=U32[D+8]=U32[P+0x20], head ordinal H=U32[D+0x0C]=U32[P+0x24], and count N=U32[D+0x10]=U32[P+0x28]. The accepted requested-key field P+0x10 is distinct.
storageBoundary.recordAndBlocks: The selected record holds two saved words, event and argument. Map entries select 16-byte blocks containing four record-pointer slots. The body does not establish the lifetime, semantic validity or which code holds, replaces and releases an object designated by the saved argument.
storageBoundary.arithmetic: For append index operations let T=low32(H+N) and Q=T>>2. The selected block index subtracts B once when Q>=B. It does not compute arbitrary modulo B. Slot offset is 4*(T&3). Full-register address additions and word index and count operations retain their native widths. Valid ordinal range, nonwrapping compatible address and size arithmetic, backed map, block and record spans and physical-alias premises remain required.

appendBoundary.order: 0x82C563B4 requests an 8-byte allocation from 0x82D3DBA0. The preserved result R is written at 0x82C563C0 and C4 with the saved event and argument, without a local null check. When (H+N)&3 is zero and B<=(low32(N+4)>>2), 0x82C563FC requests 0x822FDCE0(D,1). The continuation reloads head, count, capacity and map, computes the one-subtraction block selection, and samples its block. A zero block requests 16 bytes at 0x82C56440 and stores the returned value into a freshly loaded map at 0x82C56448. It then freshly loads the map and block again and forms the selected slot address.
appendBoundary.guardAndCount: 0x82C56460 stores preserved R only if the computed slot address at 0x82C56458 is nonzero. At 0x82C56464..0x82C5646C it freshly reads N, adds one and writes D+0x10 regardless of whether that guarded pointer store was skipped. This is P+0x28; the selected body contains no direct P+0x10 requested-key write.
appendBoundary.limits: The slot-address test is not an proof of allocator success or of map or block validity. A null block plus a nonzero within-block offset can form a nonzero address. Valid allocation, backing and preserved values, and normal helper return, are required before composing a successful append. Count increment alone proves neither a stored record pointer nor later dispatch, exactly-once delivery, finite draining or saved-argument lifetime. No invalid execution was observed.

growthBoundary.capacityAndErrorRequests: 0x822FDCE0 receives D. It compares low32(0x0FFFFFFF-B) with 1 and can request an error object through 0x821B1450 at 0x822FDD3C. That subtraction and comparison does not establish a general B<=0x0FFFFFFF invariant. The candidate is max(B>>1,8); delta starts at 1 and takes that candidate only when the selected unsigned bound permits. 0x822FDDA4 forms the full-register B+delta sum and tests that full sum for zero. Its nonzero arm has a word-zero trap guard before unsigned 0xFFFFFFFF/low32(sum), then compares the quotient with 4 and can request a second error object through 0x821B1450 at 0x822FDDE0. The byte-size request uses low32(4*sum). Under preserved well-formed bounds these widths agree; arbitrary overflow is not normalized away. Each error request has a local continuation if it returns, rather than a proved nonreturning error policy.
growthBoundary.mapRequestAndCopies: 0x822FDE00 requests 4*newCapacity bytes. Under stable compatible arithmetic and backing, let h=H>>2. The selected order requests a checked copy of old map suffix [h,B) into the new map starting at h. For h<=delta it requests the old prefix [0,h) after that suffix, then zeroes delta-h trailing entries and h leading entries. For h>delta it requests prefix [0,delta) after the suffix, requests [delta,h) into the new leading span, then zeroes delta entries after that leading span. Zero-length copy requests are skipped. These span descriptions require their bounds; arbitrary H, overflow and aliases are not silently repaired.
growthBoundary.checkedCopyLimit: Reuse xbox-hotjoin-transfer-restore.json#/nativeMemberTransferRetirementBoundary/copyRequestAndResult for 0x827F1620. Each reached request supplies equal destination capacity and byte count; the selected caller ignores the returned scalar. Null and short-span error paths can return after their own helpers without copying. Normal compatible copy completion, valid source and destination spans, appropriate physical alias and noninterference and preserved metadata remain required. No unconditional map-content preservation follows from a request or ignored return.
growthBoundary.publication: After the selected copies and zero fills, 0x822FDF2C freshly samples the old map and conditionally requests 0x82D3D9F0 at 0x822FDF38. Only after normal return does 0x822FDF40 publish the preserved new map. 0x822FDF3C freshly loads capacity, and 0x822FDF48 publishes low32(that value plus preserved delta). Matching the allocated capacity requires that the value stays unchanged across intervening calls. The body contains no direct head or count publication. Fresh metadata samples, allocator, free, copy and error effects and valid storage remain separate premises.

conditionalEmptyQueueExample.premises: Take a preserved constructor-empty queue with M=B=H=N=0, a valid manager, a compatible nonzero 8-byte record allocation, normal error and helper behavior, valid noninterfering 32-byte map and 16-byte block allocations, and required metadata and storage that stay unchanged. The example assumes these construction and preservation premises; this finding does not re-execute or independently expand the constructor.
conditionalEmptyQueueExample.deduction: The boundary condition requests growth. Delta is 8, new capacity 8 and the map request is 32 bytes. No old-map copy is needed; the reached zero fill establishes eight zero map entries under the stated backing premises. Normal continuation selects map entry zero, requests a 16-byte block, stores R at its first slot and writes count 1. This is a sufficient static path to one stored record, not observed execution, allocation reliability, delivery or arbitrary-state correctness.

errorRequestBoundary.helperOrder: 0x821B1450 samples U32[0x82F8DF10] and conditionally calls that value at 0x821B147C. It then freshly loads the preserved error object table and calls current virtual +8 at 0x821B1490, followed after normal return by a direct request to 0x82344930 at 0x821B1498. The selected callback cell is zero in the supported image only. Live callback zero, callback nonmutation, whether the object table stays unchanged and actual helper return are not yet established.
errorRequestBoundary.selectedVirtualRequests: Under preserved selected tables 0x821310F4 or 0x8211EC10, cells 0x821310FC and 0x8211EC18 both select 0x821B0D18, whose checked one-word window tail-branches to 0x82344930. That body calls the current object virtual +4 at 0x82344948, then requests 0x823448A8 with its returned value and a fixed text input at 0x82344958. If this selected +8 route returns normally, 0x821B1450 subsequently requests 0x82344930 again; this is request order, not a guarantee of duplicate output.
errorRequestBoundary.selectedValueLeaves: Selected +4 cell 0x821310F8 names 0x821B0D68. Its unsigned U32[object+0x20]<16 test returns the inline address object+0x0C; otherwise it returns U32[object+0x0C]. Cell 0x8211EC14 names 0x821B0D10, returning U32[object+4]. Current table, object and string backing, and values that stay unchanged, are required for each request. No string bytes or full tables are needed for this relation.
errorRequestBoundary.outputWrapper: 0x823448A8 first requests 0x827F67A8(0), samples the return of 0x827F8A80 and forms return+0x40 as an argument to 0x827F8248 with the first supplied input. A null second input selects a fixed fallback input. It samples 0x827F8A80 again for each of the next two +0x40 arguments and requests 0x827F8248 with the second input or fallback and a further fixed input, then requests 0x827F8470. The three returned-object samples are separate. Their actual layout, output effects and descendant returns remain unresolved. The checked wrapper has an ordinary return sequence.
errorRequestBoundary.limits: Do not name the selected chain throw, abort or terminate, or infer successful output or nonreturn. Every checked body has ordinary return or tail structure; actual descendant return and effects, callback mutation, table replacement, error-object construction and cleanup and propagation remain unresolved. The selected leaves do not establish a universal error-object layout.

deferredReaderBoundary.admissionAndFront: Reused 0x82C56550 first tests P+4 nonzero and P+0x28 count nonzero. Each iteration at 0x82C5657C freshly loads C=U32[P+4] and reads C byte +0x0C without repeating the null check. A nonzero byte exits. Otherwise it samples the queue head, capacity, map, block and front record R using a single capacity subtraction. Valid current C and all selected storage remain required.
deferredReaderBoundary.deliveryBeforePop: For nonzero preserved R it loads the two record words and requests 0x82C56478(P,Rword0,Rword4) at 0x82C565D4 before reading pop metadata afresh at 0x82C565D8. Reuse the accepted dispatcher C0, C1 and C2 relation by exact pointers: C0 supplies the null and byte checks, C1 supplies virtual +0x10, and only its zero result low byte allows C2 virtual +0x14 with event and argument. The three samples can differ and are not the reader acceptance sample.
deferredReaderBoundary.freshPopAndRetainedFree: After the dispatch returns normally, fresh count zero skips metadata pop. Nonzero fresh count increments the fresh head, resets it when the new ordinal is not below 4*fresh capacity, decrements count and resets head again on count zero. Both routes then conditionally request 0x82D3D9F0 for preserved nonzero R at 0x82C56620. Thus callback-produced count zero can skip metadata pop while still reaching the preserved-record free request. A null R skips dispatch and free but does not itself suppress a reached nonzero-count metadata pop.
deferredReaderBoundary.repeatLimit: The reader freshly tests count at 0x82C56624 and can repeat from the fresh controller load. It does not clear the selected pointer slot or free pointer blocks in this body. Original front identity, fresh pop identity, current controller, record generation and callback append and removal effects are not equated. Exactly-once delivery, finite draining, no reentry, no stale or free alias and safe retirement require additional evidence about which code holds, replaces and releases the record. No invalid execution was observed.

compositionPremises: Manager, each current controller, map, pointer block, record and any designated saved-argument object require valid appropriately sized backing and lifetime when used; these roles are not assumed nonaliasing.
Ordinary ABI, frame and nonvolatile-register value preservation, compatible allocation and free behavior and normal return of preceding calls are required for local continuation claims.
Arithmetic, count, head and capacity ranges, source and destination spans and physical mapping must support the actual selected operations. One subtraction is not arbitrary modulo.

Callbacks, constructors, checked copies, allocator, free and output descendants can affect fresh observations. Preserved and fresh generations must be linked explicitly before claiming preservation, append, delivery or reclamation.

The accepted entry-lifetime proof separates manager P, sampled controller P+4, requested key P+0x10 and header loading. This queue contract does not identify an actual current lobby controller during entry or a pump.
minimalProposal: No behavioral fix is justified by this finite static contract. A future authorized observer should remain default-off, passive and limited by a finite event cap, recording numeric request and return, record-store-guard, append count, growth and error path, byte-check, dispatcher-check, and pop and free categories at existing reads and calls. Correlate opaque local generations for manager, controller, map, block, record, error and output roles without extra getters or control-flow changes. Keep reader acceptance and dispatcher C0, C1 and C2 distinct, and request, returned helper, metadata update and observed delivery and completion separate. Emit no names, participant identities, payloads, raw pointers, credentials, code, full tables or retail text.
unrunCases: UNRUN: Valid preserved empty queue and valid preserved wrapped queue, distinguishing requested allocation and copy, actual pointer store, count update and later delivery. No model or proposed test was executed.
UNRUN: Controller byte-check exit versus accepted iteration, actual C0, C1 and C2 generations, nonzero check result and selected handler completion.
UNRUN: Naturally occurring normal allocation and storage outcomes and observed guarded-store categories. Unsupported storage, forced failure and callback-mutation behavior remain outside this result.

UNRUN: Fresh callback count zero versus nonzero, append and removal during callback, preserved R free request, which code actually holds, replaces and releases the record, and finite drain. Controls do not assert a naturally occurring defect.
UNRUN: Live callback absent or present, selected current error tables, ordinary descendant return and observed output effects, without error injection or nonreturn assumptions.
UNRUN: Game acceptance, UI completion, native or SDK leave, membership retirement, peer or transport delivery, host-wait release, cancellation and retry remain separate acceptance controls.
nextStaticOwners: If a concrete error-return discriminator is needed, select descendants 0x827F67A8, 0x827F8A80, 0x827F8248 or 0x827F8470 for their actual output-object, return and effect contract; they remain queryable beyond this finite finding.

Identify current global callback installation and mutation, and whether the actual selected error-object table stays unchanged, before composing the two virtual requests that apply only under conditions. Constructors 0x821B12C0 and 0x821C9EF8 and cleanup 0x821C9FB0 remain separate helper open questions.

Identify allocator and free outcomes, which code holds, replaces and releases the record and saved argument, and whether values stay unchanged through callback reentry, append and removal, before asserting stable growth, exactly-once delivery or safe record reclamation.

native-screen-controller-lifecycle.json is the canonical record of the selected manager update, controller publication and replacement, reader request sites and retirement requests. Actual entry and pump invocation, and which code holds, replaces and releases the preserved controller and record, remain separate relations. Reuse the queue reader proof here rather than duplicating it.
guards: No successful append or event delivery follows from count increment alone.
No direct requested-key increment, whole-state preservation, arbitrary modulo or stable controller proof is supported.
Image-zero callback data is not a runtime zero observation; selected cells do not prove that the live table stays unchanged.
No error-chain nonreturn, successful output, invalid execution, observed bug or OOM repair is claimed.
Screen-event storage and dispatch do not establish gameplay or network command delivery, membership retirement, safe cancellation or host release.
conclusion: The selected native deferred UI queue stores record pointers through a guard and then increments the count at manager P+0x28. Growth, checked-copy and error paths issue ordered requests, each made only when its condition holds; the reused reader dispatches a preserved record before fresh pop metadata and its free request. Successful storage, delivery, finite draining, current-controller identity and which code safely holds, replaces and releases records remain qualified.
diagnosticBounds: A proposed capture declares a finite event cap and dropped-event count. Overflow or incomplete pre and post pairs invalidate sequence, delivery and reclamation conclusions. Keep controller, record and storage generations distinct and preserve all original calls, inputs, returns and order.
